newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares seen edging down in post-record calm.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares seen edging down in post-record calm.

text.p: A dribble of domestic profit taking took the edge off the Russian shares market which opened lower on Tuesday morning and traders predicted low liquidity and light selling through the day and week after last week's rally.
"There is no trend -- it is calm after the sharp rise while people rethink their positions," a Regent European Securities trader said predicting the market would inch down through the week.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index opened at 554.12 after 554.20 on Monday and down from the 570.66 record set mid-afternoon last Friday, when profit-taking set in.
Traders foresaw volumes of about $50-$70 million for the day, at the edge of what is considered a healthy market and about half record daily volumes set last week.
Regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS inched up to $1.715 at 0950 GMT on the RTS from $1.705 at the previous close. Regional telecom Uralsvyazinform URSI.RTS ticked up to $0.0860 from $0.0885.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS oil company fell to $27.20 from $27.35 and southern Urals energy company Bashkirenergo was a morning price gain leader, rising to $0.910 from $0.850.
CentreInvest Securities salesman Dmitry Nikitin saw the market down up to one percent for the day on low volume and mainly domestic selling.
But he said new money was flowing into the market and second tier companies in sectors such engineering, machinery and pulp and paper. "My clients think the blue chips are too expensive."
